one_liner: Small C JIT back end (PHP 8.4+ JIT) that compiles about 40x faster than gcc -O2 for code about 4% slower.
what_it_does: A C library for building JIT compilers: you construct each function in its graph-based SSA IR through the C-macro builder API (ir_builder.h), or load it from textual IR or (with HAVE_LLVM=yes) from LLVM IR, then ir_jit_compile(ctx, opt_level, &size) runs the pipeline and returns a pointer to executable machine code. It is the code generator behind PHP's opcache JIT since PHP 8.4 and the back end of the experimental Rational C Compiler (dstogov/rcc). It is not a drop-in for gcc: the README's gcc comparison feeds it clang-produced LLVM IR.
how_it_is_fast: The IR is Sea-of-Nodes (Click) stored LuaJIT-style as one flat two-way array of nodes referenced by index (constants grow one way, instructions the other), so construction and passes touch compact memory with few allocations. Folding (constant folding, copy propagation, algebraic simplification and reassociation, CSE) runs on the fly during construction from declarative rules in ir_fold.h, hashed at build time. The pipeline is deliberately short: optional MEM2SSA, Wegman-Zadeck sparse conditional constant propagation, Click global code motion, topological local scheduling, max-munch tree-pattern instruction selection, linear-scan register allocation on SSA with second-chance bin packing (Wimmer), and DynASM emission straight into executable memory with no assembler or linker step.
when_to_use: You are building a method or tracing JIT for an interpreter, query/expression engine or DSL in C or C++ and want code near gcc -O2 quality without shipping LLVM.
Compile latency matters: hot functions or traces where LLVM -O2 compile time would eat the gain; the README reports 35-50x less compile time than gcc -O2 on oggenc, minilua, gzip and bzip2.
Your targets are x86-64, 32-bit x86 or AArch64 on Linux, macOS, FreeBSD or Windows (all in CI).
You need JIT plumbing beyond codegen: SNAPSHOT/GUARD side exits and exit groups for deoptimization, GDB JIT interface, Linux perf jitdump, graphviz dumps and textual IR save/load.
You want a production-proven back end: PHP 8.4 and later ship it as their JIT.
when_not_to_use: Peak code quality matters more than compile time: the README shows gzip at 0.80 and bzip2 at 0.81 of gcc -O2 speed; no auto-vectorizer is documented (explicit vector types and EXTRACT/REPLACE/SPLAT/SHUFFLE ops were only added in 2026) and alias analysis is still on the TODO list.
You need a stable, packaged API: IR_VERSION is 0.0.1, the README says it is 'not a stable finished product yet' and recommends embedding the sources, as PHP does.
Your target is RISC-V or 32-bit ARM: no back end (open issues #168 and #91).

You want a general C compiler: the C path is clang plus the optional LLVM loader ('partially compatible') or the unfinished RCC; long double is unsupported and by-value struct passing in registers is incomplete per TODO.
You need the lowest possible compile latency for a baseline tier: copy-and-patch designs (WasmNow, PochiVM) or TPDE aim lower; none of them is compared against IR on the same workload.

integration.form: source-drop (the Makefile also builds libir.a and an `ir` driver)
integration.dependencies: DynASM (vendored; generating ir_emit_x86.h or ir_emit_aarch64.h needs the bundled minilua compiled with a host C compiler at build time); libcapstone for the disassembler (ir_disasm.c is in the Makefile's libir.a object list and the driver links -lcapstone); LLVM optional (HAVE_LLVM=yes) for the LLVM IR loader
integration.min_toolchain: C11 (a CI job builds with -std=c11); GCC, Clang and MSVC (win32/Makefile via nmake) in CI
integration.platforms: x86-64, x86 (32-bit) and AArch64 back ends; CI on Linux x86-64, i386 and aarch64, FreeBSD amd64, macOS arm64 and Intel (ASan/UBSan), Windows (windows-2022, MSVC)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; compilation state lives in a per-function ir_ctx, but the x86 back end hands a file-static DynASM global-label array (dasm_labels) to every emit and the perf jitdump and GDB JIT hooks use process-wide state, so serialize compilations or audit before compiling from several threads

gotchas: Harness flaw behind the 40x: the compile-time table compares gcc -O2 from C source (preprocessing, parsing, SSA construction, optimization) with IR starting from clang output that, per the README pipeline of 26 Apr 2024 when the tables were last updated, had already been through LLVM's mem2reg, so front end and SSA construction sat outside IR's timed step; no CPU, gcc version, IR opt level or timing script is published, the numbers have not been re-measured since, and there is no comparison with the LLVM back end (llc), the natural baseline for a JIT code generator.

Allocation results are not checked: ir_mem_malloc/ir_mem_realloc default to malloc/realloc and ir.c uses the result directly, so out-of-memory is a NULL dereference unless you #define ir_mem_* to allocators that abort or longjmp (PHP maps them to emalloc/erealloc via ir_php.h).

Release builds compile IR_ASSERT out and do not validate input; call ir_check() in debug builds. ir_jit_compile returns NULL silently when IR_OPT_FOLDING was set for -O0 or missing for -O1/-O2, and failures report only a ctx->status code. Builder macros assume a variable named ctx (_ir_CTX) and IR should be emitted in reverse post order or folding scope shrinks.

Correctness fixes are still landing in 2025-2026, including miscompilations: #134 (diamond-to-COND produced invalid IR), #132 (COND regression), #153 (GCM hoisted PHI uses above LOOP_BEGIN), #145 (snapshot live range not extended to a GUARD) and #205 (guard reused flags across a fused memory binop, closed Sep 2026).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick IR over Cranelift and TPDE when you want a small embeddable C library (no Rust toolchain, no LLVM) with SCCP, global code motion and SSA register allocation giving code near gcc -O2; pick TPDE when your front end already emits LLVM IR and LLVM -O0-class code compiled 10-20x faster is enough, and Cranelift for Rust or Wasm runtimes; over AsmJit and sljit, IR adds a real optimizer and global register allocation rather than instruction-level emission. The PHP JIT sibling's kostya numbers are for PHP 8.2.3, before PHP moved to IR, so they say nothing about this back end.
verified_claims_summary: First-party README tables (last updated 26 Apr 2024): 18 C programs lowered by clang to LLVM IR without optimizations, loaded and JIT-compiled by IR (opt level not stated; the driver defaults to -O2) ran at a geomean 0.96 of gcc -O2 speed (0.80 gzip to 1.13 hash), and on oggenc, minilua, gzip and bzip2 IR compiled 35-50x faster than gcc -O2 (geomean 40.34). No CPU model, gcc version or benchmark scripts are published (bench/ holds only mandelbrot files), and gcc's time includes front-end work IR skipped.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-10-05) and MIT-licensed, shipping inside PHP 8.4+ as its JIT, but the author calls it unfinished with no stable library or API versioning; the README benchmark tables date from 26 Apr 2024, cannot be reproduced from the repo, and their compile-time ratio flatters IR because gcc's front end and SSA construction are counted only on the gcc side.
